title: Cache Configuration
description: Learn how to configure React Query cache settings for optimal performance and user experience.

data.text: React Query uses a two-layer cache model: the query cache stores query results, while the garbage collector removes unused queries after a configurable period. The two most important settings are `cacheTime` (how long unused queries stay in cache) and `staleTime` (how long data is considered fresh before background refetching).
`staleTime` is the freshness window. Set it higher for data that rarely changes, like a list of countries. Set it lower for frequently updating data, like a dashboard count.
data.title: Freshness vs Cache Duration

items: cacheTime: Duration in milliseconds before unused queries are garbage collected. Default: 5 minutes.
staleTime: Duration before data is considered stale and eligible for background refetch. Default: 0 (always stale).
refetchOnWindowFocus: Refetch when the user returns to the tab. Default: true.
refetchOnReconnect: Refetch when the network reconnects. Default: true.
data.title: Options
Global cache configuration
data.content: Set sensible defaults at the QueryClient level.

data.text: You can override global defaults at the individual query level. This is useful when one query needs different caching behavior than the rest.

data.title: Per-query configuration

data.text: Setting `cacheTime` too high can cause memory leaks in long-running applications with many unique query keys. Monitor cache size in production.
data.title: Memory Considerations
Cache Configuration Key Points
points: staleTime controls freshness, cacheTime controls retention.
Global defaults are set on QueryClient.
Balance memory usage with user experience.
data.takeaway: Proper cache configuration is the foundation of a performant React Query application.
